title: Penile Traction in Peyronie's Disease
summary:
Induratio penis plastica (IPP) is an acquired condition of the penis characterized by the formation of hardened areas in the connective tissue layer surrounding the erectile tissue. These scar-like changes lead to deformation of the penis. Curvature of the penis of varying degrees, as well as shortening of the penis, may occur. Over time, the condition can also lead to impaired penile rigidity and thus to erectile dysfunction. IPP occurs in approximately 3–9% of the male population, with men over the age of 50 being more frequently affected.
Studies indicate that using a traction device over several months can lead to a significant reduction in penile curvature. However, there are still too few studies, and it is also unknown whether the improvement achieved is permanent; therefore, the effectiveness of traction therapy cannot yet be conclusively assessed. We hope that the planned study will demonstrate that, in men with IPP requiring treatment, the symptoms of the condition improve with at least three months of traction therapy—compared to no treatment.
Patients in the treatment group receive a penile traction device, which applies simultaneous traction both lengthwise and against the curvature caused by the condition. For a period of 3 months, the traction device is used for a total of 30–60 minutes daily, spread over 2–3 sessions per day. The daily wear time is strictly prescribed for the first 3 months. This is followed by a 3-month period of use at the patient’s discretion. Following the completion of the 6-month treatment period, a 3-month follow-up phase begins during which the penile traction device is not used. The purpose of this phase is to determine whether any changes that may have occurred are permanent.
Patients in the control group initially receive no treatment for the entire duration of the study (9 months).

interventions.name: Penile traction using a traction device for 30–60 minutes per day over a period of three months, followed by use at the patient’s discretion for an additional three months and three months without further therapy

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Ability to understand and willingness to sign a written
informed consent form
- Diagnosis: Induratio penis plastica (N48.6)
- Curvature of ≥30 degrees in a single plane
- Chronic induratio penis plastica (stable condition for ≥ 12 weeks) that causes
significant distress to the patient
Exclusion criteria:
- Prior treatment with a traction device
Note: Previous use of a vacuum erection device does not
constitute a contraindication.
- History of surgical treatment for IPP
- History of surgery on the penis or scrotum within the last 6 weeks
- Chronic pain in the penis, testicles, or scrotum that is not related to IPP
- Skin infections and chronic open wounds on the penis or scrotum
- Congenital absence and aplasia of the penis (Q55.5)
- Other specified congenital malformations of the male genital organs
such as congenital penile deviation (Q55.8)
- Previous surgical treatment of hypospadias
- Stretched penile length <7 cm
- Erectile dysfunction that does not respond to phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors or intracavernosal
injection therapies
- Severe vascular diseases, including loss of sensation in fingers, toes, or
limbs due to ischemia
- Diabetes mellitus with signs of end-organ damage (peripheral neuropathy,
retinopathy, chronic kidney disease stage III or higher)
- Any psychological, familial, sociological, or geographical situation that could
impair adherence to the study protocol and follow-up plan
- Participation in interventional clinical trials (concurrently or within the
last 30 days)
- Private health insurance
